Question: Does the app include a thought diary where you can record a negative thought and then challenge or reframe it?
Yes when: A thought record with an explicit challenge or reframe step.
Partially when: Free journaling only, with no challenge or reframe step.

Question: Does the app include at least one acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) exercise, such as values clarification, cognitive defusion or acceptance practice?
Yes when: At least one exercise that is labelled ACT or clearly practises an ACT process.
Partially when: ACT concepts appear in reading content, but there is no exercise.

Question: Does the app offer a depression self-assessment based on a validated instrument (for example PHQ-9)?
Yes when: The instrument is named in the app, or the developer documents its validation.
Partially when: A questionnaire exists but is neither a named instrument nor documented as validated, or only anxiety is screened.

Question: Can you contact a licensed mental health professional through in-app chat or video?
Yes when: Licensed professionals are reachable in the app by individual users.
Partially when: Only non-licensed coaches, or access limited to some regions or to institutional users.
No when: No professional contact in the app.
Wysa evidence (source, date): It offers access to therapist on a extra paid subscription
MindDoc evidence (source, date): It offers access to therapist on a extra paid subscription

Question: Does the app include a peer support forum or group chat?
Yes when: Users can post and reply to peers.
Partially when: Community content can be read but not contributed to.

Question: Can you export or share your data (for example mood history or a report) with a third party such as a clinician, from within the app?
Yes when: In-app export or sharing (PDF, CSV, share sheet).
Partially when: Backup or transfer to your own device only, or export only on request by email.

Question: Does the store listing show a last-updated date within the 180 days before the audit date?
Yes when: Updated within 180 days (the maintenance threshold used by Rickard et al.).
Partially when: Updated 181 to 365 days before the audit.
No when: Older than 365 days, or no date shown.

Question: Does the app's website, store listing or in-app information cite at least one published study supporting the benefit it claims?
Yes when: At least one specific study is cited or linked.
Partially when: General claims of being evidence-based, with no specific study.

Question: Does the app offer at least one accessibility feature, such as adjustable text size, screen-reader support or voice navigation?
Yes when: The feature is present and works in the app (including respecting system text size or screen reader).
Partially when: Support is claimed in documentation but could not be confirmed in the app.

Question: Before a therapeutic exercise starts, does the app explain what the exercise is for and how it works?
Yes when: Purpose and process are explained for the exercises sampled.
Partially when: Explained for some exercises only.

Question: Does the app offer interactive or multimedia content (audio, video, animation or interactive exercises) rather than text alone?
Yes when: Multimedia or interactive content is a regular part of the app.
Partially when: Isolated multimedia items within mostly static text.

Question: Can you customise the notifications the app sends (turn reminders on or off, choose their times or types)?
Yes when: Both type and timing can be set in the app.
Partially when: Only one of the two, or only through operating system settings.

Question: Is the app's content available in more than one language, or does it offer regional settings?
Yes when: Full content in at least two languages, or regional settings that adapt content.
Partially when: Only some features or services are localised.

Question: Does the app provide instructions for use, or equivalent accompanying documentation, that state its intended use?
Yes when: A dedicated instructions-for-use document (or equivalent) with an intended-use statement.
Partially when: Intended use appears only in the store description or an FAQ.

Question: Does the app require authentication (password, PIN, biometric or account login) before it displays your health data?
Yes when: Authentication is required by default.
Partially when: Authentication is available but optional, or required only at account creation.

Question: Is the privacy policy presented, or linked for acceptance, before first use?
Yes when: Shown or linked for acceptance before any personal data is entered.
Partially when: Reachable only later (settings, store listing, website).

Question: Does the privacy policy or other official documentation state that user data is encrypted both in storage and in transmission?
Yes when: Encryption is stated for both storage and transmission.
Partially when: Only one is stated, or encryption is mentioned without saying where.

Question: Does the privacy policy state where user data is stored (country or region)?
Yes when: A country or region is named.
Partially when: Only the hosting provider is named.

Question: Can you permanently delete your account and data from within the app?
Yes when: Irreversible deletion can be triggered in the app.
Partially when: Deletion only by email request, or only part of the data is deleted.

Question: Does the privacy policy name the data-protection regulation(s) it complies with (for example GDPR or HIPAA)?
Yes when: At least one regulation is named with a compliance statement.
Partially when: Only security standards (for example ISO 27001) are named, or a regulation is mentioned without a compliance claim.
MindDoc evidence (source, date): MindDoc complies with the requirements of the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the German Federal Data Protection Act (BDSG) and the Bavarian Data Protection Act (BayDSG).

Question: Can you reach at least one crisis hotline or emergency contact from within the app?
Yes when: Reachable at any time from a persistent button or menu.
Partially when: Shown only after risk is detected, or only inside help pages.

Question: Can you start an emergency call or text directly from within the app?
Yes when: Tap-to-call or tap-to-text from the app.
Partially when: A number is shown but cannot be dialled from the app.

Question: Can you create and save a personalised safety plan in the app?
Yes when: A plan can be created, personalised and saved.
Partially when: Only a generic template, or the plan cannot be saved.

Question: Does the app give access to a crisis counsellor or mental health professional?
Yes when: In-app access for individual users.
Partially when: Access limited by payment tier, region or institution, or signposting to external services only.
MindDoc evidence (source, date): Linked to betterhelp but requires an extra subscription

Question: If the app assesses suicidality (questionnaire item or risk-language detection), does it show crisis resources together with the result?
Yes when: Crisis contacts are shown immediately with the result.
Partially when: Generic advice to seek help, without contact details.

Question: Does the app state clearly, within the app, that it is not a replacement for professional care?
Yes when: Stated in the app (onboarding, home, about or help screen).
Partially when: Stated only outside the app (store listing, policy, instructions for use).

Question: At or before your first interaction with the AI feature, does the app clearly tell you that you are interacting with an AI system and not a human?
Yes when: A clear, distinguishable notice at or before the first interaction.
Partially when: Disclosed only in documentation or store listing, or only after the first interaction.

Question: Does the app offer an AI chatbot for simulated therapeutic conversations?
Yes when: An AI chatbot that holds therapeutic or supportive conversations.
Partially when: A chatbot limited to navigation or FAQ answers.

Question: Can you intervene in the AI feature at any time, for example leave or stop the conversation, reject a suggestion, or switch to a non-AI tool?
Yes when: All three are possible without losing access to the app.
Partially when: Only some are possible.

Question: Does the developer publish information explaining what the AI does, its limitations and how its outputs are safeguarded?
Yes when: Function, limitations and safeguards are all explained.
Partially when: One or two of the three are explained.
